sections.h2: Who sets the value of a house in Greene County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The Greene County Auditor is the assessor for every parcel in the county. The auditor appraises land and buildings at estimated fair market value, and the taxable value is 35 percent of that appraisal, according to the county's appraisal page.

Greene County completes its six-year revaluation by the end of 2026, and the adjusted values show up on tax bills mailed in 2027. Between full revaluations the auditor updates values every three years. The real estate department keeps records on more than 73,000 parcels and answers questions at (937) 562-5072.

The department's own list of what it tracks shows what a seller can ask about before listing:

  • Appraised value, building description and building footprint
  • Current Agricultural Use Value (CAUV) and certified forest land reductions
  • Homestead credit, owner-occupied credit and non-business credit
  • Tax rates, reduction factors and legal description
  • Property transfers and conveyances

sections.h2: What does the Greene County housing market look like on paper?
sections.html:
Xenia is the county seat and Beavercreek is the largest city. The county covers about 414 square miles of land in the southwest part of Ohio and sits inside the Dayton metro area. Census Bureau estimates put the 2025 population at 174,322, which is 3.8 percent above the 2020 base.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied home value of $252,200 and a median household income of $87,309. Owners occupy 68.0 percent of homes. School districts that bill property tax here include Beavercreek, Bellbrook-Sugarcreek, Cedar Cliff, Fairborn, Greeneview, Xenia Community and Yellow Springs, plus the Greene County Career Center.

A seller should know which district the parcel sits in, since the levy mix on the bill follows the district and the township or city. Wright State University in Fairborn, Central State and Wilberforce universities in Wilberforce, and Cedarville University add steady rental and student demand around those towns.

sections.h2: When is Greene County property tax due, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
Ohio sets the default collection dates at the end of December and the 20th of June, and a tax commissioner order or levy timing can extend them. Read the due date printed on the current bill, because the Greene County Treasurer treats a payment as late the day after that date and grants no individual extensions.

The penalty is 10 percent of the unpaid half under R.C. 323.121. If the full amount arrives within ten days after the date, the treasurer waives half of it. Interest then runs on delinquent balances.

Active-duty service members can ask the treasurer for extra time through the Military Assistance Program. An owner who was penalized can submit the Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties (DTE 23A), which appears on the county forms page.

The treasurer also posted a notice about mail. Since late December 2025 the postmark date usually reflects the day the Postal Service machinery first handled the envelope, which can be a day or more after drop-off. Mailing early, getting a hand-stamped postmark at the counter, or using another payment method avoids that problem.

sections.h2: How can you pay the Greene County Treasurer?
sections.html:
The treasurer's office is at 15 Greene St., Xenia, OH 45385. Mail goes to the same address with a USPS postmark, since a private meter does not count. A locked curbside drop box sits in front of the building and takes checks day or night during collection periods.

  • Online through Point & Pay, with fees paid to the vendor: 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum for credit cards, a $2.95 flat fee for debit cards and $0.75 for eChecks.
  • Monthly budget plan by mail-in or electronic withdrawal, started by calling (937) 562-5289.
  • Semi-annual electronic withdrawal during normal collection periods.
  • In person at the office, or by mailing the stub with a check payable to the Greene County Treasurer.

Changing the mailing address for a tax bill must be done in writing to the treasurer under R.C. 323.13, which matters for sellers who want the bill sent to a new address after closing.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Greene County valuation?
sections.html:
File a Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property (DTE 1) with the county auditor. The auditor's page says the deadline is March 31 of the following tax year, and R.C. 5715.19 allows the later of that date or the close of first-half collection. The complaint goes to the Board of Revision, which weighs value, not tax rates.

The county's guidance for filers spells out what evidence to bring:

  • Proof specific to the property. General remarks about the market do not speak to your parcel.
  • For rental or commercial property, income and expense statements for up to three years.
  • For an appraisal, an appraiser willing to testify before the board.
  • For a sale, the realtor listing showing list price, history and days on market.
  • For condition problems, photos, completed work and written repair estimates.

A party who disagrees with the board can appeal to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the Court of Common Pleas, and the notice of appeal is due within 30 days of the mailing of the board's decision.

sections.h2: Which Greene County tax relief programs can a homeowner use?
sections.html:
The homestead reduction under R.C. 323.152 reaches owner-occupants who are 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or the surviving spouse of such a person at age 59 to 64. The statute prints a $25,000 true-value reduction figure and a $30,000 income limit, both adjusted each year, and a $50,000 figure for disabled veterans and surviving spouses of public service officers killed in the line of duty. Ask the auditor for the current numbers.

The county forms page lists the matching applications: DTE 105A for seniors and disabled owners, DTE 105B to continue, DTE 105C for the owner-occupancy reduction, and DTE 105I for disabled veterans. Other forms cover CAUV (DTE 109), destroyed or damaged property (DTE 26) and exemption requests (DTE 23 and 24). Manufactured home owners have their own set, including DTE 50.

sections.h2: What happens when Greene County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county treasurer holds the state's first and best lien on the real property. After the auditor sends over the Delinquent Land Tax Duplicate, the Greene County Prosecutor may start a foreclosure case in the treasurer's name. The treasurer's delinquent tax division can be reached at (937) 562-5672 for anyone who wants to pay the balance on a parcel already in a foreclosure action.

A seller behind on taxes usually clears the balance through the closing agent from the sale price, so an early payoff figure helps.

sections.h2: How does tax affect the sale and transfer of a Greene County house?
sections.html:
Before the recorder accepts a deed, the auditor's office transfers it. The county requires a Statement of Value (DTE 100) or its exempt version (DTE 100 EX), approval from the map department, a grantor name that matches the prior deed, and a notarized signature. The auditor's page prints the conveyance fee at $2.00 per thousand dollars of price, plus a $0.50 per parcel transfer charge, and a calculator is posted on the auditor's site.

Under R.C. 319.202 the grantor pays those charges, and the buyer's statement must say whether the seller reports a homestead reduction or CAUV status that could trigger a recoupment charge. Ask the closing agent to show how the first-half and second-half bills are split.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Greene County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Greene County Treasurer at 15 Greene St. in Xenia. A curbside drop box in front of that building accepts checks all day during collection periods, and online payment through Point & Pay adds the vendor's fee.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Greene County value?
faqs.a: March 31 of the year after the tax year in question, or the close of first-half collection if that is later. File the DTE 1 complaint with the county auditor, and bring evidence that fits your own parcel.

faqs.q: Does Greene County offer a monthly way to pay tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer runs a monthly budget plan by mail-in or electronic withdrawal, and it can be started by calling (937) 562-5289. A semi-annual withdrawal option also exists.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when a Greene County house sells?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, pays it to the auditor before the deed goes to the recorder. The county prints the rate as $2.00 per thousand dollars of price, plus $0.50 per parcel.

faqs.q: What if I mailed my Greene County tax payment on time but it was marked late?
faqs.a: Ask the treasurer about the Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties (DTE 23A). Because the postmark now reflects when the mail was machine processed, ask for a hand-stamped postmark when mailing near a due date.
